title: What Were We to Do?
craft_focus: rhetorical questions that make the reader feel the problem

source.basis: Adapted from Booker T. Washington, Up from Slavery (1901), under DESIGN_RULES 2.5.
source.attribution: Washington, Booker T. Up from Slavery. 1901. Project Gutenberg eBook #2376, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2376, accessed 2026-11-11. Public domain in the United States.
source.adaptation: Extracted a single passage; the authoring pass will split long sentences and simplify rare words; no facts added.
source.survey: A school for freed people has more students than rooms and no money to buy a campus.

license_evidence: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2376 - Project Gutenberg public-domain statement; work published 1901, pre-1929, public domain in the United States.
notes: Anchor: the two questions 'What were we to do?' and 'But how were we to get it?' The passage answers each: only a shanty and an abandoned church, then a burned plantation priced at five hundred dollars with no money. The dialect aside can be dropped in adaptation; it is not needed for the craft.
